quest.title: For the Children of the Past
quest.description: The Ashvattha Tree has been corroded. But from its fruit, Arama seems to have gained new knowledge, memories, and... manners of speech. According to Arama, you should eliminate Marana's Avatar next so that the new Ashvattha Tree may be born. Only then can the Bija be formed.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x500, Primogem x60, Mora x50000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *huff*... *huff*... You're flying too fast, Arama!

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Is that so? Sorry. But based on how you float, you shouldn't be exhausting any stamina.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon must be fully focused to fly, so it is exhausting! Arama, just fly at the speed of a Seelie, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: A Seelie? In the ancient stories, Seelie were a great race with wisdom and beauty beyond the pale of this earth. They traveled with Nara and taught Nara languages and the philosophy of nature.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Paimon thought that they were just large but annoying fireflies that lead us around by the nose...

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Seelie are just empty husks that race left behind. This is because they were born with a curse: If they fall in love with Nara, they shall lose their intelligence and strength, and their bodies will regress.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: There was once a survivor of that race deep within the golden desert who was friends with Queen Aranyani and the ruler of Valuka. Perhaps there are more stories to be found in the eternal oasis.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmmm...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Yes. So you see... at their prime, the Seelie were probably faster than a storm. Plus, isn't Paimon tired? We can rest while I tell stories about Sarva.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You even know how to be evasive now, Arama. You've really changed...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Anyway, this was our first home{RUBY#[S]Vanarana}land. Aranara used to live here before the disaster, and many Nara had visited us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Before the disaster... Are you saying that...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Yes, and you've been to the second Vanarana. Meanwhile, Marana's Avatar is imprisoned by three seals deep within this place.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Three Inscriptions of Remembrance are needed to undo the first seal. While the landscape here is a little different from the memories I received, I have a rough idea where they are.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Anyway, Marana is very dangerous. Nara {NICKNAME}, Paimon, I recommend we match each other's pace. Let me know when you're ready to set out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Three seals, and we must find three Inscriptions of Remembrance just for the first seal... This is so troublesome. Why does everything have to be done three times?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: They don't call it "The Rule of Three" for nothing...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... If Ruu were here, Paimon's sure he and Arama would become friends real quick...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Ruu?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yes, he's a friend of ours.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #I see. I too wish to meet Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon's friend. A Nara who's friends with both of you is for sure a great Nara.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: But it's alright. The past and the future meet in Sarva. A day will come when I'll have the honor of meeting this Ruu and becoming friends with him.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: By the way, there are actually four seals imprisoning Marana. The first seal is the Door of Vana, which is right behind us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! It feels like we have so much to do! Let's get moving!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Alright. We'll set out whenever you are ready.

choices.text: I wanna rest a while longer...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Alright. We'll set out whenever you are ready.

choices.text: ...Is there a reason why you told us that story?

dialogues.speaker: Mural
dialogues.text: (A slightly crude mural of Aranara with a golden Aranara among them. They seem to be happily celebrating something.)

talks.objective: Go in search of the Inscriptions of Remembrance with Arama

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What was that? Was that Ararakalari? It just...

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: No, it wasn't. Paimon needed help, so I hit the Marana very, very hard. I'm very pleased to say that I eliminated that evil tumor.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: May we never meet again, evil tumor.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If hitting a Tumor of the Withering very, very hard can destroy it, the Aranara should be able to deal with The Withering once and for all, right?

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: No, it has to be hit very, very hard, specifically. Most Aranara aren't that strong.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Many, many suns must pass, then many, many moons must pass. When seed turns to tree, when stream turns to river, only then will an Aranara possess such strength.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon gets it now. But y'know, you're speaking normally again, Arama...

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Used too much strength just now. So, many words, many memories, gone with the wind.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... Paimon remembers someone saying that memories are Aranara's bank of strength...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon was just trying to eliminate The Withering here...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: It's fine! Used energy will come back slowly. I've absorbed the Ashvattha Tree's memories, so I recover even faster. We destroyed Marana's evil tumor, very good, very good.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: The seal is nearby. Many different Ararakalari here keep Marana's Avatar in. So, it sent the evil tumor to damage the seal.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: That looks like Aradasha's stone lock...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And this... This is the flower that sealed Ashvattha's Concourse...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Oh! It's Arayama's flower. In the past, many Aranara fought Marana here, and together they sealed this place.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Marana's Avatar is very, very deep underground. Break this seal, then break the next seal, and we can face it and defeat it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whatever the case, let's do our best for a little while longer. We'll eliminate Marana's Avatar and get the Bija!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Yeah! We can do it, Nara {NICKNAME}, Paimon! I will stay and build up some strength. I need strength to face Marana's Avatar.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Oh, right! Nara "rest" so that they can build up their strength and defeat Marana! Nara are amazing!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Rest is meant to build up strength, yeah, but not everyone has to fight Marana...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Is that so? Well, luckily Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon "rested" before coming. We'll definitely defeat Marana's Avatar now!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #There are some tiny lights around us that can resist Marana's corrosion and protect Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon. You can rest if you want.

choices.text: How do we break the seals?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #I don't know... This place has changed so much, many memories lost too. I'm sorry, Nara {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Well! Solving these puzzles will be a piece of cake! Right, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course! Hehe.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh, really? Haven't we been able to solve so many puzzles and find so much treasure along the way because you're fond of puzzles...?

choices.text: So what should we do now?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Try to sense the memories within the inscription...)

dialogues.speaker: Inscription of Remembrance
dialogues.text: ...Ah, so you too are a child of the forest. Since you're reading my Inscription of Remembrance, Marana is gone, right? Or perhaps you're here to put an end to it?

dialogues.speaker: Inscription of Remembrance
dialogues.text: There are many stories I wish to hear. Is Araja's dream beautiful? Are Arana and Aramani doing well? I'm sure the new songs born into this world are absolutely beautiful!

dialogues.speaker: Inscription of Remembrance
dialogues.text: Oh, there's no rush to tell me anything. For I hear no more and see no more. But fret not, for we shall meet in Sarva.

dialogues.speaker: Inscription of Remembrance
dialogues.text: When the time comes, you can take your time to tell me the stories of the earth! This inscription is the work of Araji, Arayama, and myself — our pride and joy. It's yours now...

dialogues.speaker: Inscription of Remembrance
dialogues.text: "May the new dre{RUBY#[S]Vanarana}ams never experience Marana's corrosion."\n"And may the old sto{RUBY#[S]Vanarana}ries be forgotten alongside it."

talks.objective: Continue searching for the Inscriptions of Remembrance

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Arama! We're back! How are you feeling?

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Oh! I've built up some strength! I'm fine! I can sense that the seal is broken. Now, leave the rest to me.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: There's so much sand here. I think it used to be stone and soil. But Marana took away the life and moisture in the soil, turning it into sand.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Aranakin hates sand. If only he could see this!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: See what?

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: See sand vanish!

talks.objective: Obtain the second Inscription of Remembrance

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Try to sense the memories within the inscription...)

dialogues.speaker: Inscription of Remembrance
dialogues.text: Araji really wants to see Vanarana filled with many, many flowers again, and birds on green trees while Nara sing with us under the trees.

dialogues.speaker: Inscription of Remembrance
dialogues.text: Marana really is terrifying, but thinking about scenes like that makes it less scary. Arayama said that Araji is very brave, and that Araji should think about happy things when afraid.

dialogues.speaker: Inscription of Remembrance
dialogues.text: So Araji decided on the inscription's content, with the hopes that it will bring courage to you who have come to Vanarana that is beautiful no more...

dialogues.speaker: Inscription of Remembrance
dialogues.text: "May the green fields and mountains never wither."\n"May the streams stay clear and the flowers remain in bloom."

talks.objective: Continue searching for the Inscriptions of Remembrance

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There aren't any clues...

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: I see. But this place is very calm, very good.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah. But it must be really difficult for you to keep the ring up and fend off The Withering, Arama...

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #I'm fine! Being with Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon is a very happy thing. I won't forget!

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: I recovered some strength while resting, so I remember now! This used to be Aramuhukunda's home!
#Hello, Arama, Nara {NICKNAME}, and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Where did you come from...

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: You're Aramuhukunda...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Aren't you that mysterious Aranara we met during Festival Utsava? That Aranara who speaks unlike any other Aranara?

response.speaker: Aramuhukunda
response.text: #You still remember. That gladdens me. Nara {NICKNAME} made a garland from my flower and the flowers of many Aranara. To me, that is a great honor.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Aramuhukunda! I've heard so many stories about you, and I played with you in the memories of Arayama and the others!

response.speaker: Aramuhukunda
response.text: Then you've inherited their memories, I see. As a past friend of theirs, this fills me with pride.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Yes... But during the battle her{RUBY#[S]Old Vanarana}e, many memories vanished, like fruits falling to the ground or clouds blown away by the wind...

response.speaker: Aramuhukunda
response.text: I see. They won't be sad about it, and you have no reason to either. There's no end to the precious memories you can create and the strength you can gain while you're with your friends.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Yeah, I understand...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Arama was really impressive when he took down that Tumor of the Withering with just one punch! He did the same to a Ruin Grader too! He really helped a lot!

response.speaker: Aramuhukunda
response.text: Very good, Arama. It's just as I heard in Sarva... You're a brave Aranara.

response.speaker: Aramuhukunda
response.text: #Nara {NICKNAME}, Paimon, you've come. Intentional or not, it fills me with great pride. I've always wanted to hang out with Nara friends here.

choices.text: Do you know how to break the seal?

response.speaker: Aramuhukunda
response.text: Worry not, I know why you're here. The Ashvattha Tree told me many things, before it used what strength it had left to give Arama the fruit of dreams.

response.speaker: Aramuhukunda
response.text: Go through that cave and you'll arrive at the place where we defeated and sealed Marana hundreds of years ago. It hasn't fully recovered yet, but there's no time to lose.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Yeah! We've gotta break the last seal and defeat it as soon as possible! Only then can a new Ashvattha Tree grow to produce the Bija.

response.speaker: Aramuhukunda
response.text: And I am the final seal. I am the one who's keeping an eye on Marana's Avatar, and yet its strength still seeps through the sand like water, creeping through Sarva.

response.speaker: Aramuhukunda
response.text: I will undo this last seal and open the path for you. I'm certain that you can defeat it and put an end to this final enemy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Alright! {NICKNAME}, Arama, the seal's gone! Thanks, Aramuhukunda!

response.speaker: Aramuhukunda
response.text: #Do not worry. Rather, it is I who should say thank you. Nara {NICKNAME}, Paimon, I have a question for you before you go...

response.speaker: Aramuhukunda
response.text: I've been busy preparing an environment comfortable for Nara, just for your visit. But I've not traveled alongside Nara for far too long, so I do not trust my own judgment.

response.speaker: Aramuhukunda
response.text: #Nara {NICKNAME}, Paimon, do you like this place?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hmm... It's really nice and relaxing. There isn't anything to eat, but Paimon thinks it's pretty nice! What do you think, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Aramuhukunda
response.text: #...You're not very fond of talking, quite unlike Nara Varuna. {M#She}{F#He} kept talking about {M#her}{F#his} {M#brother}{F#sister}. {M#She}{F#He} was a terrible example for Arapacati and the others.

response.speaker: Aramuhukunda
response.text: If I have time, and with your help, I can definitely do better. But based on the current circumstances, I'm afraid time is of the essence for you and the Nara friend you want to help.

response.speaker: Aramuhukunda
response.text: My only regret is meeting you in an age like this one.

response.speaker: Aramuhukunda
response.text: Or I should say that, had we met in another age, I could have introduced Nara Varuna to you. How wonderful that might have been.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #But I wouldn't have been able to meet Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon if they came from a different age!

response.speaker: Aramuhukunda
response.text: Indeed. So this is fine. It was a little short, but I'm still very happy to have had a conversation with you. Thank you.

response.speaker: Aramuhukunda
response.text: #Nara {NICKNAME}, Paimon, go on ahead. I have something to give to Arama.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #...I understand. Nara {NICKNAME}, Paimon, please go on ahead! I'll be right behind you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, be quick, or we'll defeat Marana's Avatar on our own!

choices.text: Can't say I have any particular feelings on the subject...
Sorry, but we have other matters to attend to...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yes, let's hang out later! But we've gotta break the seal here and defeat Marana's Avatar first.

response.speaker: Aramuhukunda
response.text: You still remember. That gladdens me. You made a garland from my flower and the flowers of many Aranara. To me, that is a great honor.

talks.objective: Obtain the third Inscription of Remembrance

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Try to sense the memories within the inscription...)

dialogues.speaker: Inscription of Remembrance
dialogues.text: We will be victorious. The living will overcome the dead, and we'll meet again one day in Sarva.

dialogues.speaker: Inscription of Remembrance
dialogues.text: "Friends will stroll through the forest again. That which is good will return, and the painful memories will vanish. Just like a stream purifying itself or a withered tree sprouting once more."

dialogues.speaker: Inscription of Remembrance
dialogues.text: ...This is my inscription. Goodbye.

talks.objective: Go to the seal with Arama

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this the seal? What a huge tree hollow...

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #Yes, it's all thanks to you that I've been able to witness Old Vanarana, and lay eyes on our original home. Thank you, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: ...Thank you, Aramaha, Araji, and Arayama, thank you for guarding the seal. Marana eventually managed to escape to the outside world, but it's not your fault.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Now, I shall undo the seal which has existed for hundreds and thousands of moons...

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: May the new drea{RUBY#[S]Vanarana}ms never experience Marana's corrosion, and may the old stor{RUBY#[S]Vanarana}ies be forgotten alongside it.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "May the new dreams never experience Marana's corruption, and may the old stories be forgotten alongside it."\n"May the green fields and mountains never wither. dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The seal's been lifted! Is the path forward... downward?

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Yeah, the second seal is up next. Let's go.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Before the disaster... Are you saying that...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Yes, and you've been to the new Vanarana. Meanwhile, Marana's Avatar is imprisoned by three seals deep within this place.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Three Inscriptions of Remembrance are needed to undo the first seal. While the landscape here is a little different from the memories I received, I have a rough idea where they are.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Anyway, Marana is very dangerous. Nara {NICKNAME}, Paimon, I recommend we match each other's pace. Let me know when you're ready to set out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Three seals... It feels like we have so much to do! Let's get moving!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Alright. We'll set out whenever you are ready.

choices.text: I wanna rest a while longer...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Alright. We'll set out whenever you are ready.

choices.text: ...Is there a reason why you told us that story?

talks.objective: Try to destroy the Tumor of the Withering

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #Nara {NICKNAME}, would you like to rest?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Aradasha is very strong. In the stories, a very, very long time ago, there was once a metal beast the size of a mountain, and it could spit fire like shooting light beams.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: But Aradasha bested the beast and imprisoned it with a lock of stone! He saved many Aranara!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: His legend was as dazzling as the sun, and many Aranara wished for their Ararakalari to be as powerful as his!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: It was very scary! Even the sky turned black. Trees swayed like a field of grass under strong winds, and they all fell to the ground. And then very, very scary monsters were everywhere.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Many of the monsters in the memories I obtained look very much like the monsters we've seen. Like the black dogs, the huge metal beasts, and the hilinara.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Marana appeared during the disaster too, and many grasslands were turned to sand. That's why we fought Marana and sealed its avatar underground.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: The seal was made by many Aranara. We... They wanted to imprison Marana and stop it from harming Aranara, Nara, and the earth.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Later on, Marana slowly seeped into the ground like water. But we were in the dreams already and unaware that it had turned out so terrifying...

choices.text: No. Let's get it over with first.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Alright! Thank you, Nara {NICKNAME}, and good luck!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon never thought that there'd be such a deep space beneath the sands...

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: The earth is made of soil, stone, sand, and tree roots. So if sand is removed, a very, very large space will appear. Aranara, Nara, and animals can move within it.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: But more sand should have vanished to make more space and let us go deeper. Bad sand.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon saw many ruin machines while descending... So a fierce battle really did occur here...

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Yes. The monsters here and the monsters in the Ashvattha Tree's dream, I've seen them in the memories too — the black dogs and huge metal beasts.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's look for a way to go further down!

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Okay!

talks.objective: At least, it proves to be a way down

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #Nara {NICKNAME}! Paimon! I'm glad you're alright!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Yeah! Paimon's fine! But {NICKNAME} always has it rough! Are you alright?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon didn't expect to see a space like this here... Paimon doesn't sense The Withering either...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #This should be the final seal. Thank you, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon, for coming here with me. Marana's Avatar should be close by now.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Once we defeat Marana's Avatar, I'll plant a new Ashvattha Tree, and then it'll produce the Bija for us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then let's finish this! We'll help Rana and complete Arana's request.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Yes!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: But I don't have enough memories. I don't know how to undo this seal...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry, it's not a big place. Paimon's certain we'll find something if we look around!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Arama, you rest and build up your strength! You'll need it if you plan to fight Marana's Avatar!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Alright! I'll rest well!

dialogues.speaker: Mural
dialogues.text: (A mural of many Aranara with their fronts — or backs — facing something strange. There's a golden Aranara with them.)

dialogues.speaker: Chair
dialogues.text: (This looks like a very ordinary chair.)

dialogues.speaker: Chair
dialogues.text: (...But both its size and workmanship clearly indicate that it's meant for humans, and not for Aranara.)

dialogues.speaker: Baggage and Books
dialogues.text: (It looks like something you'd see in an adventurer's camp. But the books are full of crooked drawings, mostly of Aranara doing something.)

dialogues.speaker: Baggage and Books
dialogues.text: (Speaking of which, why are adventurers so fond of bringing a stack of books with them when they go camping? Never mind the fact that their tents are open in all directions and block neither wind nor rain... Why must they bring a stack of books?)

dialogues.speaker: Aranara House
dialogues.text: (This seems to be the home of some Aranara, and looks just like those houses in Vanarana. But its "owner" is nowhere to be found.)

dialogues.speaker: Aranara House
dialogues.text: (If Aranara don't need to rest, why do they need houses?)

dialogues.speaker: Vine Thicket
dialogues.text: (Vines that have completely sealed the path off. There doesn't seem to be a way through.)

dialogues.speaker: Pool
dialogues.text: (Cool and clean water. It's impossible to tell where the water came from.)

dialogues.speaker: Mural
dialogues.text: (A mural of some Aranara forming a circle.)

dialogues.speaker: Mural
dialogues.text: (Four Aranara, one golden Aranara, and a column... Or is that a tree trunk? It's hard to tell since the drawing is rather vague.)

dialogues.speaker: Mural
dialogues.text: (...The scene looks somewhat familiar.)

dialogues.speaker: Mural
dialogues.text: (A mural of three Aranara and a golden Aranara. They seem to be entering a huge whirlpool.)

talks.objective: Go to the deepest part of the cave

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #Nara {NICKNAME}, Paimon, I recommend we match each other's pace. Let me know when you're ready to set out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Three seals... It feels like we have so much to do! Let's get moving!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Alright. We'll set out whenever you are ready.

choices.text: I wanna rest a while longer...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Alright. We'll set out whenever you are ready.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Bad sand. Rough and coarse. Ugh, green grass won't grow from it.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: There's a very, very huge Valuka outside the forest, and there are Nara in it. Nara must be suffering.

dialogues.speaker: Mural
dialogues.text: (A mural of many Aranara with their fronts — or backs — facing something strange. There's a golden Aranara with them...)

dialogues.speaker: Mural
dialogues.text: (No, there seems to be a change in the mural. There are two golden Aranara now.)

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #If only Nara {NICKNAME} was here very, very long ago. Then you could have fought the huge metal beasts with Aramuhukunda, Aradasha, and the others!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #While Nara {NICKNAME} was fighting just now, I could sense that the huge metal beast was very bad. It absorbs Marana's strength and grows stronger.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #It would be exhausting for Nara {NICKNAME} if the battle went on. Then I remembered! In my memories, Aradasha used this Ararakalari to trap and destroy many huge metal beasts.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: So, I tried his Ararakalari, and I hit it very, very hard.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: I don't know. This place doesn't exist in the memories I received. It feels like the home of Aranara, but it shouldn't be like this...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: But this place is very good. No Marana, and there's water, light, and grass.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Yes! This place is very good. We can rest.

dialogues.speaker: Aramuhukunda
dialogues.text: ...I'm glad that you understand. Arama, help your friends, and let the new Ashvattha Tree become the anchor of Aranara's dreams once more.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: I'll live up to your legacy. Aramuhukunda's name has filled us with courage since many, many moons ago, and that will not change for many, many moons to come.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: We will defeat Marana's Avatar. With your memories, I hear everyone call out to you, and it fills me with more than just courage, with pride as well.

dialogues.speaker: Aramuhukunda
dialogues.text: I believe in you. Like clouds know they have to release rain, the rain knows that it must fall onto the ground. Meeting all of you made me realize... that the time has finally come. I'm very happy.

dialogues.speaker: Aramuhukunda
dialogues.text: Now, I can finally return to Sarva and meet Nara Varuna again.
